en: Homage to the Noble and Holy Tārā,
the Mother Who Saves. Translated by Ngawang Tashi, Abbot of Beijing Jingzhu Monastery.
Protector who delivers from all diseases and transgressions, I pay respectful homage and praise before Tārā.
In the center of a pure white lotus, upon a moon-disc seat spread above it, she sits manifesting in the vajra-paryaṅka posture;
To the Mother who bestows boons, I pay respectful homage.
With a face like the radiance of the autumn moon, the Mother of Buddhas rests upon the wheel of the white orb;
all her ornaments are perfectly complete. Holding an *utpala* flower, she stands before me in respectful salutation;
her physical form is fully perfected as a sixteen-year-old, the daughter of all the Perfectly Awakened Ones.
Victorious one, you personally hold and bestow according to desire; I pay homage before the Noble Mother, the Savior.

She possesses the radiance of a pure white wheel, white in color, upon whose eight spokes appear the eight syllables, all of which exhibit the characteristic of universal rotation. Facing this wheel, I approach and pay my deepest respect.
All buddha-fields are completely pure, And within them are strewn many precious flowers.
Born as the mother of all Buddhas of the three times, Before this Noble Mother, I pay respectful homage.
To the Holy Mother Tārā, the Savior, The Mother who Increases Longevity, and the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel.
I pray fervently before the Mother of Buddhas: To dispel for us the obstacles to longevity, the afflictions of disease, and all hardships;
Relying on your power, grant me protection and the supreme and ordinary accomplishments, Bestowing them all upon me without exception.
Those who stand before the Noble Mother with sincere reverence, she constantly remembers them all as her own children;
before the Noble One, I too offer this prayer: I pray only that you ever hold us with the hook of compassion.
The Victorious Mother’s sublime body is like the color of the moon, elegant, gentle, and upright in its majesty.
Adorned with exquisite marks and arrayed in precious ornaments, she wears a lower garment of fine silk.
Seated upon a lotus and moon-disc throne, her two feet are locked in the vajra-paryaṅka posture.
With one face and two arms, her countenance is joyful; she is the mother who gives birth to all Buddhas of the three times.
I have always knelt before the Venerable Mother; now, before the Venerable One, I offer this humble praise.
May all obstacles and adverse conditions encountered while we cultivate the path from now until the attainment of Bodhi be eliminated, and may we obtain abundance in favorable conditions.

Oṃ dadāre tudatadāre rema ma āyur-labhu naye tsani ya ānabhus-tsing-kulu-ye svāhā. This mantra was transcribed according to the corrections made to the *Complete Mantras of the Imperially Commissioned Tripitaka*. This hymn was requested by the Tibetan monk Lobzang Samten from two venerable Dharma masters at the Lobsa Ling Hall within the Byes Phang Monastery. It is said to have been spoken by the Buddha.
The Praise to the White Tārā is completed.
